data.narrative:
Stellaria is a seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Nicolas Breyton and backed by CEA and Schneider Electric, having raised €23M to date. The nuclear energy sector comprises 3 public comparables (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Nano Nuclear Energy, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Fuse Energy.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable valuation method. Using total capital raised (€23M) as a proxy for current value and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to next-stage rounds yields an implied valuation of €58M. This method is grounded in observed progression patterns for early-stage capital deployment rather than statistical peer comparison. Peer-median analysis could not be applied: while 5 nuclear energy peers exist in the comp universe, the narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, similar valuation tier) yielded fewer than three datapoints, making sector-wide medians unreliable for this specific stage.

The analysis supports a triangulated range of €49M (low) to €66M (high), with a median point of €58M. This range reflects a single applicable methodology, introducing material uncertainty. Key sensitivities include the robustness of the 2.5x stage multiplier for frontier nuclear (which may differ from broader venture benchmarks) and the absence of direct peer-to-peer valuation anchors. Resolution of these uncertainties would require expanded comp availability at Seed stage or forward-looking metrics on development pathway and regulatory milestones.
